s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of involuntary movements in an elderly patient with a history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus
salient_findings: Involuntary movements of the left upper and lower limbs
Slow response and reduced muscle strength in the left limbs
Positive tendon reflexes in the left limbs
High-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia on brain MRI
key_facts: The patient is an 80-year-old woman
She has a history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus
She presented with involuntary movements of her left upper and lower limbs for more than 10 days
She had a slow response on neurological examination
She had reduced muscle strength in her left limbs
She had positive tendon reflexes in her left limbs
Her blood glucose level was 8.59 mmol/L
Her hemoglobin A1c was 7.43%
Noncontrast CT of the head showed slightly increased density in the bilateral striatal regions
Brain MRI demonstrated high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia

raw.rationale: The patient's history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus, combined with the presence of high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia on brain MRI and slightly increased density in the bilateral striatal regions on noncontrast CT of the head, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hemiballismus
rejected.why: Hemiballismus is characterized by involuntary, violent, and large-amplitude movements, which does not exactly match the patient's presentation of continuous, irregular involuntary movements of variable amplitude.

rejected.label: Fahr's disease
rejected.why: Fahr's disease typically presents with bilateral basal ganglia calcification, which is not mentioned in the patient's imaging results.

rejected.label: Idiopathic basal ganglia calcification
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by calcification in the basal ganglia, which is not consistent with the patient's imaging findings of high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images.

rejected.label: Chorea-acanthocytosis
rejected.why: Chorea-acanthocytosis is a rare genetic disorder characterized by chorea and acanthocytosis, which is not mentioned in the patient's presentation or laboratory results.
